chapter_theme: The wedding hall is dressed in gems, the lord of the city calls his daughter Sayambavai, who goes through the palace to her mother, is adorned, and sets out on the vimana with her guard, her goods and the king's army.

cast.role: the lord of the city, father of Sayambavai
the king's daughter, who is sent out to her wedding
the maidens who keep the gate
the learned men who judge the hour

851.reading: Winged birds and the Vidyadhara and Mithuna gods crowd above the wedding hall, whose red sparks fill the sky and keep the fierce sun off.
851.nuance: The first two lines are clipped and the subject of the verbs is not clear; the verse is read as the opening picture of the hall.

852.reading: The hall is dressed with gold banana trees and emerald areca palms, gem-hung gate pillars, pearls strewn on the sand and full pots.

853.reading: Gate-leaves bound in gold and pinned with diamond-tipped studs hang with gold chains and rows of ringing gems.

854.reading: Gem-strung crystal doorways and steps shine like cloud-skimming hills and show their forms to those who come before them.
854.nuance: The last line, with its word for honey-rows, is obscure.

855.reading: The floors are painted with gold dye, smeared with pearl paste and set with gems so that every corner shows clearly.

856.reading: The stage where dancing women perform, the pavilion floor and the gold door-frames beside it are likewise fitted out.

857.reading: The hall's gems are told as a flowering tree: emerald as sprouts, diamond as shoots, pearl as buds, gold as blossom.
857.nuance: The image makes the building a wishing-tree, which verse 858 names outright.

858.reading: The hall opens like a wishing-tree among the gods' own vimanas, and the lord of the city says that his daughter Sayambavai should come.
858.nuance: Only the last line is speech; the first three still describe the hall, and the verse joins the two.
858.event: The city's lord summons his daughter Sayambavai to the hall.

859.reading: Told by the girls who keep the gate, the princess comes down like a flowering creeper from her crystal chamber and couch, as a peacock descends.
859.event: Sayambavai comes down from her upper chamber when the gate-girls announce the summons.

860.reading: The king's daughter, wearing the victory garland, walks out from the tall mansion like lightning among cloud.
860.event: Sayambavai walks out of the mansion.

861.reading: Armed women and others with unripe breasts guard her sides and wish her long years, as she walks with a stately gait.
861.nuance: The guard here is of arms and numbers, set round a girl who is being sent out to be chosen.
861.event: Maidens guard Sayambavai and bless her as she walks.

862.reading: Passing the gates of the girls' city and its scented pool-stair, she goes straight to the palace where the queen sits.
862.event: Sayambavai goes to the queen's palace.

863.reading: With the women who guard her fragrant body she reaches the feet of the first mother.
863.nuance: The word for the first mother is read as the queen, since the house is the city lord's.
863.event: Sayambavai reaches the queen and bows at her feet.

864.reading: The lady of the house takes the bowing girl into her arms, smells her scented hair and sinks in a sea of joy.
864.nuance: The lady is taken as the queen; the sea of joy is hers.

865.reading: Thinking heavy gold would hurt her waist, Sayambavai is dressed in light gold, flowers and eye-paint, and made cool like a creeper in the shade.
865.nuance: The last words are obscure and who dresses her is not named.
865.event: Sayambavai is adorned for the vimana.

866.reading: The hour and its signs are looked over, learned men speak, and the speaker says that she may now climb the vimana.
866.nuance: Who says the last words is not named; the lord of the city is the likely speaker.
866.event: On the learned men's word of the hour, the king bids Sayambavai board the vimana.

867.reading: With women, nurses and chamberlains guarding her, she goes to the shining vimana like a goddess of the world above.
867.event: Sayambavai goes to the vimana in escort.

868.reading: Two thousand maidens learned in magic arts, loyal to her, guard the girl on all sides with drawn swords.
868.nuance: Verses 861 and 868 set a guard of arms round the girl.
868.event: Two thousand maidens take guard round Sayambavai.

869.reading: Her playthings, balls, parrots, dolls and mynas, are carried to the vimana.
869.event: Her toys are carried to the vimana.

870.reading: Garlands, cloth, chests, sandal and boxes of paste are loaded with them.
870.event: Her garlands, cloths and perfumes are loaded.

871.reading: Chests and treasure fill the chambers of the vimana, and it moves off with its light around it.
871.event: The vimana, loaded with her goods, sets out.

872.reading: Drums, conches and war-horns sound, horses and elephants crowd in, and the king rides an elephant's neck in glory.
872.nuance: The lines are printed as eight half-lines and were joined.
872.event: The king rides out at the head of the procession.

873.reading: Elephant bells, conches and horse-drums roar like the sea as the host leaves by the city gate, with banners trembling.
873.nuance: The lines are printed as eight half-lines and were joined.
873.event: The army sets out through the city gate.

874.reading: Swords gleam, elephants are held back, and the learned king's great host spreads shining through the sky.
874.nuance: The subject of the last line is taken as the king 'of faultless learning'.
874.event: The army fills the sky around the vimana.

links.note: Kural 57 holds that guarding women by confinement is no use and their own steadfastness is the best guard; verse 861 sets armed women round the princess.
links.teaches: The pair shows the guard of arms as outward show beside the inward guard the couplet values.

gains.a: The verse lacks a measure of what really guards the girl; the couplet gives one.
gains.b: The couplet lacks a concrete household that does guard its women by force; the verse supplies one.

links.note: Cintamani 1344 has jewelled women standing guard round the bride before her wedding; verse 868 posts two thousand armed maidens round the princess.
links.teaches: Both epics guard the bride with women, but this one makes the guard an armed troop of the magic-learned.

links.note: Cintamani 1344 has the astrologer fix the day; verse 866 has learned men judge the hour before the girl boards.
links.teaches: The pair shows the wedding hour as a learned decision in both Jain epics, with the Soolamani making it the king's cue to act.

links.note: The Silappathikaram sets Kannaki's wedding under a pearl canopy on diamond pillars; verse 852 hangs gems and pearls on a hall.
links.teaches: The pair shows the same jewelled hall at two scales: a city wedding and a palace one dressed like the gods' own.

gains.a: The Soolamani hall lacks any rite; the Silappathikaram unit gives the fire and the blessing.
gains.b: The Silappathikaram canopy is only a canopy; the Soolamani hall grows into a wishing-tree.

links.note: Kural 761 calls a complete army the chief of a king's wealth; verse 874 shows the host as a spreading display round a bridal vimana.
links.teaches: The pair shows that the host here is wealth on show, not strength at work as the couplet rates it.

gains.a: The verse lacks any test of whether the host is the king's strength; the couplet gives one.
gains.b: The couplet lacks the sight of an army spent on a wedding escort; the verse gives it.

source_issues: Verses 872, 873 and 874 are printed as eight half-lines and were joined into four; verse 862 had a pulli after a vowel sign removed.
